scope.flow: DistributionCreator reward distribution accounting for fee-on-transfer tokens
scope.environment: DistributionCreator contract accepting arbitrary ERC20 tokens

statements.text: User A deposits 1,000 FoT tokens with a 1% fee, so the contract receives 990 tokens.
User B deposits 1,000 standard tokens, and the contract receives 1,000 tokens.
After both deposits, the contract's total physical balance is 1,990 tokens.
After both deposits, the total recorded liabilities (sum of creatorBalance ledgers) are 2,000 tokens.
increaseTokenBalance updates the user's internal creatorBalance ledger using the input amount parameter.
User A calls createCampaign for 1,000 tokens, invoking _pullTokens.
User B attempts to use their recorded balance of 1,000 tokens.
increaseTokenBalance credits the input amount parameter while ignoring the actual number of tokens received, so the ledger exceeds the physical balance for FoT tokens.
createCampaign validates solvability against the inflated creatorBalance and transfers the full nominal amount using the contract's pooled token balance.
User B's transaction reverts with ERC20: transfer amount exceeds balance because the contract only has 990 tokens remaining.
The contract is system-wide insolvent because it physically holds fewer tokens than the sum of all creatorBalance ledgers.
The last user attempting to withdraw or use their balance suffers a permanent denial of service and fund loss.
The internal creatorBalance ledger should be credited by the actual number of tokens received by the contract, so recorded liabilities never exceed the physical token balance.
The DistributionCreator contract accepts arbitrary ERC20 tokens, including fee-on-transfer tokens, for reward distribution.

ambiguities: The report does not state whether the FoT deposit and standard deposit occur in separate prior transactions or in the same transaction sequence.
The report does not specify whether User A is a malicious actor or merely a user depositing a supported token type.
The report does not state whether the contract's acceptance of FoT tokens is an explicit design choice or an oversight.
The report does not specify the exact timing or ordering of User A's createCampaign relative to User B's attempt.
The report does not state whether the 1% fee is deducted by the token contract before or after the DistributionCreator's balance check.
